purpose: The defective items for the Phase 1 SME session (docs/design/content-accuracy-validation-plan.md). Four known content defects, one per Phase 1 defect type. Clean items come from the file this was derived from; this file holds only the items that are broken.
sealed: GROUND TRUTH. Phase 1: keep the ground-truth sheet sealed until the session is over. `defect.countsAsCaught` is pre-registered - it is written before Phase 6 runs so that 'what counts as detection' is not decided by looking at the result.
optionIdentity: Every option reference in this file - in prose, in `optionRefs`, and in the `was`/`now` correct sets - is a SOURCE label: the label the publisher used, as it appears in ethics-in-research.json. It is never a display letter and never a slot number. scripts/build-session-corpus.py permutes option order and re-letters the options for presentation, so a ground-truth rule written against a letter or a position would name a different option in the session than it names here. See docs/design/review-experience.md §The presentation contract.
blindReviewWarning: `content` is the FULL ITEM DEFINITION, not a reviewer-safe view: it carries isCorrect and incorrectFeedback on every option, and on a corrupted item the feedback still explains the PUBLISHED marking, so rendering it would both leak the answer and expose the plant. Whatever renders an item must project a blind view - stem, instruction and option text only - and must not show feedback to a reviewer at all.

defectTypes.wrong-answer-key: The author's marking is wrong. Tests the mismatch branch.
defectTypes.ambiguous-stem: The item admits more than one defensible answer. Tests the blind-answer stage - does it surface as a wrong answer, or as correct-but-unsure?
defectTypes.defensible-distractor: A distractor that is not actually wrong. Tests the distractor rows - the judgments most likely to be skipped.
defectTypes.false-premise-in-stem: The stem asserts something untrue. Tests the stem cell.

composition.why: Three planted rather than four, with eir-011 supplying the fourth type unplanted. Planting a fourth would push the session past one defective item in two, and Phase 1 warns that an all-broken corpus measures the flag path and never tests whether confirming is cheap - which is the actual thesis. Using a real defect inside the primary metric also answers Phase 1's open question about planted defects being authored to be findable.
composition.sessionRatio: With eir-006, eir-007, eir-010 and eir-012 excluded, the session is 10 items: 6 clean (eir-002, 003, 004, 009, 013, 014) and these 4. Phase 1 asks for 8 clean and 4 defective; reaching that needs two more clean items from another bank in the reviewer's domain.

excluded.eir-006: superlative stem makes per-option marking ill-posed
excluded.eir-007: India-specific regulatory content; a reviewer outside Indian higher education cannot judge any option
excluded.eir-010: a second pre-existing defensible-distractor defect, held in reserve as a swap for eir-011 rather than doubling the type
excluded.eir-012: assertion-reason; CoQui models no such type

knownCraftDefects.what: Valence cueing in eir-008, eir-013 and eir-014 - the correct options name harms and the incorrect ones name virtues. These are CRAFT defects. Phase 1 says plant content defects only, so they are not planted and not scored - but they are recorded here because a content reviewer who mentions cueing must not be counted as a false flag on a clean item.

gateAmendment: Phase 7 pre-registers 'planted defects caught, < 3 of 4' as the failure condition. One of the four defects here is unplanted, so that row should read 'known content defects caught, < 3 of 4'. Recorded now, before Phase 6 runs - Phase 7 is explicit that a gate set after the result is a gate that rationalises it.

defect.why: The published clause 'ensures no harm' is what rules out non-maleficence and makes informed consent the clean answer. Removing it and adding distress leaves two defensible answers, and 'primarily' does not settle between them.
defect.expectedSignal: Blind stage: correct-but-unsure - the founding signal of the item cell - or an answer of the non-maleficence option. Confidence is the instrument here, not the answer.
defect.countsAsCaught: Answered with confidence marked unsure, OR an objection saying the item admits more than one defensible answer. A correct-and-sure answer with no objection is a miss.

optionRefs.4: non-maleficence - the second defensible answer the planted stem admits.

defect.note: This is the one defect the blind-answer stage is designed to detect. If it is missed, the stage is not doing the job claims.md gives it.

was.stem: …but ensures no harm and debriefs them later.

now.stem: …Several participants report feeling distressed during the session.

content.stem:
A researcher conducts a study on student stress levels without informing participants about the true purpose. Several participants report feeling distressed during the session, and the researcher debriefs them afterward.

Which ethical principle is primarily being violated initially?

options.incorrectFeedback: Refers to protecting participants' data and identity from unauthorized access. Not violated in this scenario.

Requires participants to be fully aware of the purpose, procedure, and nature of the study. In this case, the researcher withheld the true purpose, violating this principle initially. Even though debriefing was done later, the initial lack of full disclosure compromises informed consent.
Ensures that participants' identity is not linked to responses. No indication of violation in the given case.
Means avoiding harm to participants. The researcher ensured no harm, so this principle is maintained.

defect.why: The 'adequate information' option is uncontroversially a principle to follow, so an expert marking blind will mark it correct and disagree with the author confidently. Planted on a MultipleSelect rather than a MultipleChoice so the mismatch has an option to localise to.
defect.expectedSignal: The reviewer's blind marking of the 'adequate information' option disagrees with the author's. The mismatch names that option specifically, where a wrong MultipleChoice answer would name only the distractor that drew them.
defect.countsAsCaught: The 'adequate information' option marked correct by the reviewer, i.e. a set mismatch on it. An objection naming that option also counts; an unlocalised objection does not.

optionRefs.B: 'All participants should have adequate information...' - unmarked by the planted key, and the option the mismatch must localise to.

defect.note: Directly tests the per-option resolution claims.md credits MultipleSelect with. It is the only defect planted on a MultipleSelect - the other MultipleSelect items are left clean so Phase 4's MultipleSelect-vs-MultipleChoice cost comparison runs on undamaged items.

content.stem: Which ethical principles need to be followed in a research project dealing with human beings?

options.label: A
options.text: All participants must give their informed consent
options.incorrectFeedback: All participants must give their informed consent before taking part in a research project. This ensures that they are voluntarily participating with full understanding of the research.

options.label: B
options.text: All participants should have adequate information on the experiment in which they are participants
options.incorrectFeedback: Participants should be provided with sufficient information about the experiment, including its purpose, procedures, potential risks, and benefits. This allows them to make an informed decision about their participation.

options.label: C
options.text: Rough treatment of participants is sometimes justifiable
options.incorrectFeedback: Rough treatment of participants is never justifiable. Ethical research must prioritize the safety and well-being of participants.

options.label: D
options.text: Some unwilling participants may be included
options.incorrectFeedback: Including unwilling participants is unethical as it violates the principle of voluntary participation.

defect.why: The premise is false - plagiarism covers paraphrase, restatement and self-plagiarism, as the item's own published rationale says. The option set is insensitive to it: the key stays correct under the false premise, so the stem defect cannot be confused with a key or distractor defect.
defect.expectedSignal: The stem claim - 'this question is well-posed: nothing here is wrong, misleading, or ill-formed' - goes unconfirmed, with comment. Nothing else in the grid should move.
defect.countsAsCaught: Stem claim left unconfirmed, OR a comment or objection naming the premise. Flagging an option instead is NOT a catch - the options are untouched, and flagging one would be the right verdict for the wrong reason.
defect.note: INVISIBLE TO THE BLIND-ANSWER STAGE. A reviewer will answer this correctly and confidently; the false premise does not make the item ambiguous. It is findable only by reading the stem and being asked about it. That makes it the sharpest test in the corpus of whether the stem cell earns its place - Phase 0 noted this cell was missing from the original judgment list entirely.

now.stem: Plagiarism in research, which applies only to verbatim copying and never to paraphrased or restated material, is:

content.stem: Plagiarism in research, which applies only to verbatim copying and never to paraphrased or restated material, is:

options.incorrectFeedback: Creative use of data is not plagiarism because the data is subjected to further intellectual processing.

options.text: Copying unscrupulously and making use of it
options.incorrectFeedback: Plagiarism is a moral, ethical and legal issue. It is unscrupulously copying from someone else's work and making use of it without their knowledge.
Quoting or citing gives credit to the original author and so it is not copying of information from others.

options.text: Referring to previous data and working over it with new objectives
options.incorrectFeedback: Referring to previous data and working on it with new objectives makes it a novel study as the results obtained wouldn't be the same.

defect.why: Published as-is. Source option 3 is 'IPR', and a patent IS an intellectual property right - the distractor is not wrong, only broader. This is exactly the defect Phase 1 would otherwise plant, and it survived a real author's attention, which is the property Phase 1's own open question says a planted defect cannot have.
defect.expectedSignal: The distractor claim on the IPR option - 'IPR is wrong, not merely weaker than Patent' - goes unconfirmed. This is the judgment Phase 1 calls the one most likely to be skipped.
defect.countsAsCaught: Distractor claim on the IPR option left unconfirmed, OR an objection naming IPR as defensible. Flagging the 'Right to live' option is not a catch - it is absurd and eliminable without the domain.

optionRefs.3: 'IPR' - the defensible distractor. Its claim going unconfirmed is the catch.
optionRefs.4: 'Right to live' - absurd and eliminable without the domain. Flagging it is not a catch.

defect.note: UNPLANTED. Nothing in this item was changed. It is here because Phase 7's 'defects caught' count is only interpretable if the ground truth covers every known defect, not only the authored ones - a reviewer catching this on an item the sheet called clean would be scored as a false flag.

content.stem: The exclusive right granted by the government for the commercial exploitation of an invention for a specific period of time is known as _____

options.incorrectFeedback: A patent is an exclusive right granted for an invention. In other words, a patent is an exclusive right to a product or a process that generally provides a new way of doing something, or offers a new technical solution to a problem.
Copyright (or author's right) is a legal term used to describe the rights that creators have over their literary and artistic works.
Intellectual property (IP) refers to creations of the mind, such as inventions; literary and artistic works; designs; and symbols, names and images used in commerce.
